entry.description: The activity of a Docusign organization (envelopes, templates, accounts, users and logins) and Docusign Monitor's security alerts, as logs, read every five minutes from the Monitor API with the organization's own Docusign app.
entry.name: Docusign
entry.setup:
Docusign Monitor (a paid add-on) must be enabled for the organization.

1. In Docusign (**Settings → Apps and Keys**, as an organization administrator), **Add App and Integration Key**,
   e.g. `ObserveCraft Monitor`. Copy the **integration key**.
2. Under **Service Integration**, **Generate RSA** and copy the private key (Docusign shows it once).
3. Add a **Redirect URI** to the app (any URL you control; Docusign only redirects there after consent), and enter
   it below.
4. Copy your **User ID** (the administrator's, on the same page): requests impersonate this user.
5. Save the connection, then open **Grant consent** below as that user and accept: the app may then act for them
   without a password (JWT grant). An organization administrator can instead grant consent for the whole
   organization in Docusign Admin.
6. For production accounts, the app must have passed Docusign's go-live review; demo (developer) accounts work at once.

**NetBird** connects devices, servers and cloud resources over a WireGuard® overlay network. This dashboard shows the peers of the connected NetBird account (connected or not, last seen, expired logins, client versions) and its audit log: who added or removed peers, changed policies, routes, DNS and networks, created setup keys or invited users.

- **Custom Headers**: `DD-API-KEY: {{ api_key }}`

Vercel tests the endpoint when the drain is created; the ingest key in the header authenticates its deliveries.

**Traces.** Add another drain of type **Traces** for the same projects, with **Custom Endpoint**
`{{ intake }}/v1/traces`, format **Protobuf** (or JSON) and the same header. Spans arrive as OpenTelemetry traces
(APM); logs written during a traced request carry its `traceId` and `spanId`.

entry.description: The jobs of every recipe of a Workato workspace as logs (with the recipe and project they belong to), and the recipes (offline, lifetime tasks) and connections (authorization failed or lost) as metrics, read with an API client's token.
entry.name: Workato
entry.setup:
1. In Workato, open **Workspace admin → API clients**, create a **client role** with these Developer API
   permissions: **Projects** (list projects and folders), **Connections** (list), **Recipes** (list, get, list
   versions), **Jobs** (list jobs, get job), **Tags** (list).
2. Create an **API client** with that role and copy its token; Workato shows it once.
3. Pick your workspace's data center (the host you sign in at).

streams.description: Every finished job of every recipe (service:jobs): id, title, status, is_error, error_parts, started_at, completed_at, duration, with recipe (id, name, description, folder_id, tags, job_succeeded_count, lifetime_task_count) and project (id, name, description, folder_id). Jobs still running are read once they end.
streams.name: Recipe jobs

streams.description: Every recipe's state: workato.recipes.failure (1 while the recipe is stopped, with its stop_cause) and workato.recipes.task_count (its lifetime tasks), tagged name, recipe_id, stop_cause, workato_tags, project.

metrics.description: 1 while the recipe is stopped (stop_cause says why when Workato stopped it), else 0.
metrics.name: workato.recipes.failure

metrics.description: The recipe's lifetime task count.
metrics.name: workato.recipes.task_count

streams.name: Recipes

streams.description: Every connection's state: workato.connections.failure (1 when its authorization isn't successful or Workato lost it), tagged name, provider, authorization_status, authorization_error, connection_lost_reason and active_recipes (whether a running recipe uses it).

metrics.description: 1 when the connection's authorization failed or Workato lost the connection, else 0.
metrics.name: workato.connections.failure

entry.description: The audit log of a Zero Networks Segment account (segmentation, rules, JIT and MFA access, API tokens, admin logons) and, when filtered, its network activities (connections allowed and blocked between assets) as logs.
entry.name: Zero Networks
entry.setup:
1. In the Zero Networks admin portal, open **Settings → Integrations → API** and select **Add new token**.
2. Give it the **Read Only** access type and an expiry, then copy the token; the portal shows it once.
3. Network activities are many: to collect them, copy the filters of a view of **Activities → Network** (for
   example blocked traffic only) into **Network activity filters**, then turn the stream on.

streams.description: Every audit event (service:audit): record.auditType with its label in fields_mapping.auditType, record.performedBy (the user or token), record.enforcementSource, record.userRole, record.details, record.destinationEntitiesList.
streams.name: Audit

streams.description: The network activities the configured filters select (service:network-activities): record.src and record.dst (asset, IP, port, process, user), record.protocol, record.trafficType and record.state with their labels in fields_mapping. Off by default: set the filters first, an unfiltered account sends every connection.
streams.name: Network activities

entry.name: ZeroFox Cloud Platform
entry.setup:
1. Sign in to the ZeroFox platform as a user of the enterprise account who can see its alerts.
2. Open **Settings → Data Connectors → API Data Feeds** and create (or copy) your **API token**.

streams.description: Every alert raised or changed (one log per change): id, alert_type, rule_name, severity (1–5), status, network, offending_content_url, perpetrator, asset and entity, assignee, tags, escalated, logs (the alert's history).
